events.title: Roman annexation of Thrace
hints: A client kingdom was turned into a province after its last king died in AD 46.
Mines and fertile plains made the Thracian lands valuable to the empire.
events.summary: After the death of King Rhoemetalces III in 46 AD, the Roman emperor Claudius annexed the Thracian kingdom as a province. Roman cities, roads and military camps spread across the territory until it passed to the eastern empire.

events.title: Byzantine conquest of the First Empire
hints: A long war against a medieval tsardom ended with the Emperor nicknamed the Bulgar-Slayer.
Rebellion in 1185 restored a medieval empire after about 170 years of rule from Constantinople.
events.summary: After decades of war, Emperor Basil II ended the First Bulgarian Empire in 1018 and its lands were absorbed into the Byzantine Empire. Byzantine rule, with heavy taxation, lasted until the Asen and Peter uprising of 1185.

events.title: Ottoman conquest and rule
hints: The Danube stronghold of Nikopol fell in 1396 after a failed crusade.
Roughly five centuries of rule ended after the Russo-Turkish War of 1877 and 1878.
events.summary: The Ottomans conquered the Bulgarian lands in the late 14th century, ending the medieval tsardoms. Rule lasted until the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–78, which led to an autonomous principality under the Treaty of Berlin.

events.title: Suppression of the April Uprising
hints: Irregular troops crushed a rebellion in the Rhodope and Balkan mountains in spring 1876.
Reports of killings in the village of Batak shocked Europe and stirred outcry in Britain.
events.summary: Ottoman irregular forces suppressed the April Uprising of 1876, destroying villages and killing thousands of civilians; estimates vary. The atrocities drew wide European condemnation and helped lead to the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–78.

events.title: Treaty of Neuilly
hints: A Paris suburb gave its name to a 1919 treaty that cost the loser its Aegean coast.
The army was capped at 20,000 men and reparations of 2.25 billion gold francs were imposed.
events.summary: Under the Treaty of Neuilly of November 1919, Bulgaria ceded Western Thrace, which cut it off from the Aegean, along with border areas to Yugoslavia. It also had to pay reparations of 2.25 billion gold francs and limit its army to 20,000 men.

events.title: Soviet occupation and satellite regime
hints: The Red Army crossed the Danube in September 1944 and a Fatherland Front coup followed.
One of the Warsaw Pact's most loyal members, it even floated joining the USSR in the 1960s.
events.summary: Soviet forces entered in September 1944, and a communist-led government took power. The country became one of the most loyal Soviet satellites, with its economy and foreign policy closely tied to Moscow through Comecon until 1989.
